newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street shares seen steady at market open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street shares seen steady at market open.

text.p: Wall Street shares are expected to open mixed to steady on Monday, somewhat cautious at the start of a week replete with U.S. economic data.

While no economic data are due today, stocks and bonds should move gingerly in anticipation of upcoming reports, including Tuesday's second quarter employment cost index and Friday's employment data, analysts said.
Technology stocks are expected to be particularly active following reports on the personal computer market and news of an acquisition by chipmaker Intel Corp.

"There will be a lot of news this week focused on inflation at all levels," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "With earnings season winding down, the focus will shift to the economic numbers."

In addition to the employment cost index report and the employment data, this week's data calendar includes the July consumer confidence survey on Tuesday, and the second quarter gross domestic product growth estimate, due Thursday.
"It looks like we'll open on a mixed to steady note," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities.
In early trade, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index rose 2.30 points to 947.20.
The long bond gained 2/32 to a yield of 6.45 percent.
The dollar was firm after surging to a seven-and-a-half year peak against the mark overnight.
Shares of semiconductor and personal computer stocks will draw attention today, analysts said.
Intel's announcement that it plans to acquire Chips and Technologies Inc for $17.50 cash per share, or about $384 million, could enliven chipmaker stocks, they said.
Shares of personal computer makers could get a lift from reports indicating the sector showed robust worldwide growth in the second quarter.
Dataquest, a market research firm, said worldwide PC unit shipments rose 17 percent in the quarter from a year earlier. It said Compaq Computer Corp extended its lead in market share.
International Data Corp, another market research firm, also said Compaq remained the world's top PC vendor.
"Reports showing the PC business surged in the second quarter could get the box makers moving," Wachtel said.

The dollar was trading at 117.10/15 yen. In Europe, the dollar rose to set a fresh 7-1/2 year high against the mark at 1.8473 marks. It was boosted by prospects of a weak European single currency and sound U.S. economic growth.
Japan's Nikkei average closed up 185.72 points, or 0.91 percent, at 20,575.26.
In London, the FTSE 100 was up 3.5 at 4855.0.
U.S. stocks were mixed in London trading.
